response: Delayed peripheral facial palsy in stapes surgery can be prevented. The condition is likely caused by the reactivation of the herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1), which is latent within the geniculate ganglion. This reactivation is more frequent in patients with a history of herpes labialis. To prevent delayed peripheral facial palsy, adequate acyclovir therapy can be administered. This treatment has been shown to be effective in reducing the risk of this complication in patients undergoing stapes surgery.
